basis:
WHAT THIS FILE IS. The observed ENVELOPE of every entry the speed gate measures, recorded from six dispatches of one tree on the cell that reads it: ubuntu-latest, image ubuntu24/20260927.320, runner 2.337.0, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure. Each dispatch ran ROUNDS=2 and the two rounds within a dispatch agreed to about 2%; n records the six dispatch-level observations the min and max below were taken from, so if a future re-measurement has the per-round values split out, n and the envelope are re-derived together rather than widened by hand. No number here is invented, and each traces to a dispatch summarised for this file: the runner figures were reported from dispatches of the tree recorded in measured_commit, and the instrument was chosen by the probe in counter.py, not assumed. measured_at is when this document was written, not when the dispatches ran.

WHY AN ENVELOPE AND NOT A SINGLE VALUE. CPU seconds exclude steal, so a co-tenant does not reach them — that is what makes them a valid magnitude where elapsed time is not. They are still hardware-dependent: a faster or narrower core runs the same instructions in fewer CPU seconds, and the ubuntu-latest pool spans instance types. Measured here, one tree over six dispatches spread 58.8% (unit suite: 10.287820 - 16.340854), 61.3% (bench.render: 0.055953 - 0.090278), 83.6% (bench.render-impact: 0.770657 - 1.414891) and 60.1% (bench.render-responsiveness: 0.054544 - 0.087334), and the whole vector moved together — the fastest run was 35-40% below the slowest on every entry at once, which is a property of the machine and not of the code. A single stored value plus a budget wide enough to cover that would need a tolerance above 1.0 on some entries, which is not a loose gate but a gate that cannot fire. So each entry records the range it was actually observed over, the head must clear observed maximum x (1 + tolerance), and the down-only ratchet acts on that recorded maximum: an improvement lowers the ceiling, and a regression has to clear the worst machine actually seen.

WHY THE TOLERANCE IS 0.25 IN BOTH POPULATIONS, AND WHAT THE GATE THEREFORE IS. The recorded maximum already contains the entire observed spread, so the tolerance covers what was NOT observed rather than repeating it. 0.25 is a quarter on top of the worst run observed: it will let an occasional worse-than-anything-seen run through rather than red on a machine the pool surprises us with, and it is far below the ~2x that a genuine step change produces. STATED PLAINLY SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER: this is a STEP-CHANGE DETECTOR, NOT A REGRESSION DETECTOR. It catches a doubled workload and an accidental quadratic. It will not catch a 20% regression, and the phrase 'load-invariant counter' does not license reading it as a sharp budget. Both populations take the same fraction because their ceilings are both 'the worst machine observed, plus a quarter', and the numbers that differ are in the ceilings, not in the fraction.

WHAT IS NOT HERE. `wall` is empty: no wall observations were supplied with these dispatches, so the gross smoke gate is off rather than armed against a guessed number. When wall figures are collected they go in that map, and the smoke gate starts comparing against them without any other change.

HOW TO RE-DERIVE. Run the job several times on the cell that will read it — at least three, since a two-dispatch envelope is thin — and take each entry's min and max across those dispatches, with n counting them. Re-derive, never carry: an envelope recorded on one machine and applied to another is the mistake this schema exists to make impossible, and it is why the ratchet refuses any raise to a recorded maximum.
